about: Mutants of hosts/opentui (the schema of hosts/mygo's ledger). Each edit is applied to a copy of the module's file, then the killers run. A killer is dir:Test, where dir is a directory of this Go module (hosts/opentui/<pkg>).

mutants.name: OT0-fetch-no-integrity
mutants.from: if err := CheckIntegrity(data, want); err != nil {
mutants.to: if err := CheckIntegrity(data, want); false && err != nil {
mutants.rule: a tarball whose bytes differ from the pinned sha512 integrity is refused before it is read

mutants.name: OT0-no-struct-size
mutants.rule: every record carries its struct_size (bindc's autofill); OpenTUI refuses one without

mutants.name: OT0-any-abi
mutants.rule: Load refuses a library of another ABI version; the check is generated, so a hand edit is refused

mutants.name: OT1-destroy-leaves-children
mutants.rule: Destroy removes the whole subtree, children first, so no handle of it stays

mutants.name: OT1-move-ignores-index
mutants.rule: Move puts the node at its index among the parent's children

mutants.name: OT1-chunk-drops-escape
mutants.rule: an escape sequence cut between two feeds is one key, not Escape and text

mutants.name: OT1-resize-not-passed
mutants.rule: Resize resizes the renderer, so the scene lays out at the new size

mutants.name: OT1-off-owner-thread
mutants.rule: every library call runs on the owner thread

mutants.name: OT1-close-no-drain
mutants.rule: Close writes the terminal's restoration before it frees the session

mutants.name: OT2-tab-reversed
mutants.from: if back { (at + n - 1) % n } else { (at + 1) % n }
mutants.to: if back { (at + 1) % n } else { (at + n - 1) % n }
mutants.rule: Tab moves the focus to the next focusable node in tree order, Shift+Tab to the one before

mutants.name: OT2-hit-stops-at-text
mutants.rule: the mouse goes to the nearest node that takes input above the scene's hit, not to a text inside a Pressable

mutants.name: OT2-insert-ignores-before
mutants.rule: an Insert puts the node in front of its Before, in the driver's tree and on the scene

mutants.name: OT2-set-text-not-sent
mutants.rule: a Set of a text sets the scene node's text

mutants.name: OT2-remove-leaves-screen
mutants.rule: a Remove destroys the node's scene subtree

mutants.name: OT2-disabled-takes-focus
mutants.rule: Tab passes over the nodes under a disabled Fieldset (a press under it does nothing: the session drops it, ui Fieldset)

mutants.name: OT2-no-reveal
mutants.rule: a tap on a row below a Scroll's fold scrolls it into view first

mutants.name: OT2-window-prints-start
mutants.to:
out.Println("0: \(counter.Summary(tui.StateOf(&d)))")
		for i, act in steps {
mutants.rule: the terminal binary prints what the example's own binary prints, and nothing more

mutants.name: OT2-key-names-collide
mutants.rule: no two key codes have one name

mutants.name: OT2-cells-off-by-half
mutants.rule: a whole multiple of the cell is exactly that many cells

mutants.name: OT2-unsafe-outside-edge
mutants.rule: only ot/ and screen/ import unsafe or C

mutants.name: OT3-backspace-takes-last
mutants.rule: Backspace deletes the grapheme before the caret, not the last one

mutants.name: OT3-ctrl-w-no-boundary
mutants.rule: Ctrl+W deletes back over spaces, then over one word, and stops at the space before it

mutants.name: OT3-paste-keeps-newlines
mutants.rule: a paste into a field has its newlines as spaces

mutants.name: OT3-set-drops-caret
mutants.rule: a Set from the program keeps the caret's cell where the new text reaches it, else puts it at the end

mutants.name: OT3-cells-as-bytes
mutants.rule: a caret's offset counts cells (a wide rune two, a combining mark none), not bytes

mutants.name: OT3-ctrl-k-kills-start
mutants.rule: each editing key makes its edit (routing rule 3)

mutants.name: OT3-tab-caret-stays
mutants.rule: a field reached by Tab has its caret at the end (not where it was, the start after a Set)

mutants.name: OTL-reply-dropped
mutants.rule: a terminal's reply to the setup's queries reaches the session, which learns from it that the terminal takes notifications

mutants.name: OTL-notify-silent
mutants.rule: Notify on a terminal writes the notification (OSC 9 where the terminal takes it), not only keeps the text

mutants.name: OTL-set-unsaid
mutants.from:
case ui.Set[E] as x:
			try sayLive(d.s, x.Node)
mutants.to:
case ui.Set[E] as x:
			let _ = x
mutants.rule: a live region set to a new text says it, as ui.TestHost announces it

mutants.name: OTL-insert-unsaid
mutants.from:
case ui.Insert[E] as x:
			try sayLive(d.s, x.Node)
mutants.to:
case ui.Insert[E] as x:
			let _ = x
mutants.rule: a live region a step shows with a text says it, as ui.TestHost announces it

mutants.name: OTL-empty-said
mutants.rule: an empty live region says nothing

mutants.name: OTL-first-pass-said
mutants.rule: the first pass, the view as it starts, says nothing, as ui.TestHost and a page's live region

mutants.name: OT4-row-at-written-index
mutants.rule: a list's written row i is placed First + i rows down its content, not i

mutants.name: OT4-viewport-not-reported
mutants.rule: a list's viewport is reported to the session (ui.Scrolled) when it changed, so the next pass writes the rows it shows

mutants.name: OT4-wheel-misses-lists
mutants.from:
case ui.ScrollNode, ui.RowsNode:

mutants.rule: a turn of the wheel scrolls the Scroll or the list under the pointer

mutants.name: OT4-capture-ends-on-move
mutants.from:
case Some[ui.Id[E]] as a:
		try point(d, a.Value, input, ui.Moved)
mutants.rule: an Area that a Down went to holds the pointer until an Up, through moves

mutants.name: OT4-pass-rebuilds-the-scene
mutants.to:
for k in kidsOf(d, d.root) {
		d.s.Destroy(numOf(d, k))
		unnumber(d, k)
		rebuild(d, k)
		attach(d, k, d.root)
	}
	placeRows(d)
mutants.rule: a pass changes the scene where its ops say, never by building it anew: a row added costs the same library calls at any list length

mutants.name: OT4-zone-never-over
mutants.rule: a pointer event on an Area carries the topmost Zone under the pointer and its box in the Area's box (Point.Over)

mutants.name: RK-pass-offset-ignored
mutants.rule: a list shows the offset its pass chose (RowsNode.Offset: RowsKeeping brings a row into view)

mutants.name: OT5-transform-dropped
mutants.rule: a canvas paints under the transforms in effect (PushTransform)

mutants.name: OT5-fill-even-odd
mutants.rule: a canvas fill covers what its path holds under the nonzero rule

mutants.name: OT5-picture-at-the-corner
mutants.rule: a canvas's picture shows at its box's place in the frame

mutants.name: OT5-tick-paints-unchanged
mutants.from:
let ops = try ui.Step(&d.session, ev)
	if len(ops) > 0 {
mutants.to:
let ops = try ui.Step(&d.session, ev)
	if len(ops) >= 0 {
mutants.rule: a step (a frame's Tick among them) whose pass changes nothing shows nothing: no library call, no byte

mutants.name: OT5-frames-while-settled
mutants.rule: the driver steps a Tick only while the view animates, as ui.TestHost's Advance does

mutants.name: OT5-edge-scroll-still
mutants.from:
let (_, at, next) = x.Value
		next != at
mutants.to:
let (_, at, next) = x.Value
		next != at && false
mutants.rule: while an Area holds the pointer near an edge of the list inside it, each frame scrolls the list by ui.EdgeScroll, as ui.TestHost's Advance does

mutants.name: OT5-edge-scroll-plain-scroll-still
mutants.rule: an Area holding the pointer near an edge of a plain Scroll inside it (and no list) edge-scrolls the Scroll each frame by ui.EdgeScroll, as it does a list

mutants.name: OTPH-move-areas-only
mutants.from: try point(d, under(d, targetAt(d, input.X, input.Y)), input, ui.Moved)
mutants.rule: a move goes to the node under the pointer whatever its kind, so leaving every Area (or moving over a child that is not an Area) crosses as on TestHost

mutants.name: OTTOT-kind-wildcard
mutants.to:
ui.ZoneNode, ui.SemanticNode[E], ui.LayerNode[E]:
		screen.Box
	case _:
		screen.Box
mutants.rule: every match over ui.Node in the terminal host names each kind, so a kind it does not name is a check error, not a quiet box (the mutant brings back a wildcard and drops TrackNode; the killer is the totality guard TestTuiMatchesNameEveryKind)

mutants.name: OTUL-feed-records-len-plus-one
mutants.rule: SessionInputFeed passes the records slice's own length, so the library writes no record past it

mutants.name: OTUL-read-output-len-plus-one
mutants.rule: SessionReadOutput passes the buffer's own length, so the library copies no byte past it

mutants.name: OTUL-resolved-chars-len-plus-one
mutants.rule: LeaseResolvedChars passes the buffer's own length, so a buffer one byte short of the cells is refused, not overrun

mutants.name: OTUL-term-size-swapped
mutants.rule: termSize reads the kernel's winsize in its layout: columns from ws_col, rows from ws_row

mutants.name: OTUL-cell-past-the-edge
mutants.rule: Screen.Cell reads the lease's planes only within its width × height; a column at the width is outside

mutants.name: OTMR-input-named-by-placeholder
mutants.from: if x.Label != "" { Some{Value: x.Label} } else { Some{Value: x.Placeholder} }
mutants.rule: the terminal names an Input as ui.Find does: its field label when it has one, else its placeholder (todo-tui's LabelledField "new item")

mutants.name: OTMR-label-first-of-many
mutants.rule: tui.Play fails ui.Ambiguous where two nodes share the label a step names, as ui.Play does, instead of taking the first (todo-tui's items of one name)

mutants.name: OTSEM-disabled-focused
mutants.to:
case ui.SemanticNode[E] as x:
		ui.Focusable(ui.SemanticNode[E]{Access: ui.Named(ui.Radio, ""), On: x.On, Style: ui.Plain()})
mutants.rule: a disabled Semantic takes no focus: the terminal's focus order is ui.Focusable's (Tab skips radio d)

mutants.name: OTSEM-semantic-not-pressed
mutants.from:
// option, a link), as std ui takes it (OT-SEMANTIC).
		ui.Focusable(n)
mutants.to:
// option, a link), as std ui takes it (OT-SEMANTIC).
		false
mutants.rule: a click on a Semantic that sends, or Enter on it focused, sends its signal as on TestHost

mutants.name: OTRD-reserve-shown
mutants.rule: a Readout shows its reading, not its reserve

mutants.name: OTRD-published-not-painted
mutants.rule: a Publish shows on the screen with no pass: the driver paints the nodes that read the readout on its Published

mutants.name: OTRD-box-by-reading
mutants.rule: a Readout's box is its reserve's width whatever it reads, so its siblings never move
